subject: Using posterior samples as prior in new model

messages.author: 249ba2bf0beed132
messages.subject: Using posterior samples as prior in new model
parts:
Hi Nimble Devs,

First, thanks for the great package. I find NIMBLE to be very useful and flexible.

I have been working on a problem with the goal of a complete accounting for uncertainty. The data arise in a way such that a "cut" distribution is needed (i.e. in the posterior the posterior conditional for variable B depends on variable A but the posterior conditional for A does not depend on B).

I can fit this model without fully accounting for uncertainty by first fitting the model for A and using the posterior mean of A (A_bar) to sample from [B|A_bar]. If I were to code this model by hand, I would first run the MCMC for A (without B) and get L posterior draws of A. Then, the pseudocode for MCMC iteration (k) out of K when sampling B is

1. Sample A^(k) from the first stage model fit posterior independent of the current MCMC state
    - A^(k) is a random sample from {A^(1), ..., A^(L)} ( In R: A <- A_posterior[sample(1:L, 1)])

2. Update B^(k) using A^(k) 
    - B ~ [B| A^(k)]

Is there a way to do this in NIMBLE by passing the posterior of A as data and then using the sample function in R? For example, the non-working MWE


## Nimble Model
library(nimble)
code <-  nimbleCode({
  mu <- mu_post[sample(sample_vec, 1)]
  for (i in 1:N) {
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu, sigma)
  }
  sigma ~ dunif(0, 100)
})


## simulated data
N<- 100
y <- rnorm(N, 2, 3)

## "first state model fit"
L <- 1000
mu_post <- rnorm(L, 2, 0.01)

dat.fit <- list(y=y, mu_post=mu_post)
constants.fit <- list(sample_vec=1:L, N=N, L=L)
dimensions.fit <- list(mu_post=L)

model_fit <- nimbleModel(code, data=dat.fit, constants=constants.fit, 
                         dimensions=dimensions.fit, 
                         check=TRUE)

parts:

I'd like to clarify what you are trying to do.

Do you want the posterior of A to be sampled as a prior for mu in model B?

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Using posterior samples as prior in new model
parts:
Ok.  What I'm trying to clarify is "use the posterior distribution... to estimate sigma in the second model."

I know you're non-working MWE is intended as a sketch to convey the idea, but I'm not sure what "mu <- mu_post[sample(sample_vec, 1)]" is supposed to mean.  BUGS is a declarative model language.  A deterministic node normally doesn't do something stochastic (although there's nothing in nimble preventing it), and it won't be recomputed unless its parent nodes change, which apparently won't happen after sample_vec is set once.  If what you want is that in the model for sigma (which you call B in the generic description), mu follows the posterior of the first model, you might be looking for 

mu ~ dcat(mu_post[1:L], uniform_probs[1:L])

where uniform_probs are all set to 1/L.

Note that you can build both models and then set the data in the second model at a later step.  Unlike BUGS and JAGS, you don't need to provide the data at the outset.

If the sampling of mu is inefficient, one could make a new sampler, say that draws from nearby values of mu in mu_post.

Let me know if that helps or if the real problem is different.

Perry

messages.author: 249ba2bf0beed132
messages.subject: Re: Using posterior samples as prior in new model
parts:
Thanks Perry,

That's getting close to what I want, but in what you propose, the distribution of mu will be updated in model 2 using the distribution of sigma. I only want to account for the uncertainty about mu from model 1 without the estimate from mu being influenced from the data.

What I was trying to convey with the syntax

mu <- mu_post[(sample_vec, 1)]

is that, for each MCMC iteration in model 2, a draw of mu from the posterior of model 1 would be selected. Then, using this draw, the distribution of sigma could be updated. 



What I can do now is  replace the above statement with

mu <- mean(mu_post)

and sample sigma using the mean of the posterior of mu as known. Doing so, I don't account for the parameter uncertainty from model 1. My goal is to propogate this uncertainty forward without allowing the distribution of mu to be influenced in model 2. This is similar in idea to 

Plummer, M. (2015). Cuts in Bayesian graphical models. Statistics and Computing, 25(1), 37-43.

where I don't want the inference of sigma to "contaminate" my inference in mu.

Hi John

I've done something similar before in R using my own implementation of the IA2RMS algorithm 
http://oa.upm.es/36432/1/INVE_MEM_2014_194086.pdf

I don't have nimble code for the IA2RMS, but, if that algorithm was written for nimble, it would be relatively easy to set up a sequence of samplers that would respect the cut constraint.

Best
David

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Using posterior samples as prior in new model
parts:
Hi John,

Martyn's paper suggests using multiple imputation (i.e., separate chains each based on a draw from the posterior for mu). But it sounds like you're trying to do something somewhat different - at each iteration, change the value of mu.  If you reimpute mu at a given iteration, your current sigma may not be a good value for that value of mu, so it's not clear to me that it's a good idea to do what (I think) you are trying to do. Now if one knows the full conditional for [ sigma | mu, y] and can do a conjugate update, then it would be fine because each draw of sigma would be fully consistent with the value of mu that was used at that draw, but I'm not sure whether the model you showed in your post is the actual model of interest.

chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Using posterior samples as prior in new model
parts:
I will comment on the nuts and bolts without regard to the statistical wisdom.

I think you could use nimble's ability to customize samplers to achieve what you are describing.

Specifically, you could make a sampler for mu that ignores stochastic dependencies when sampling a new value.  It would still need to update stochastic dependencies after a value is chosen.

We could support you in implementing that, but first I suggest looking in the manual and package source code for guidance.  And also considering carefully if this is really what you want to do.

Perry
